title: KV-store TTL stalls and eviction-window jitter investigation and follow-up
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
During a capacity surge on 2025-02-18 some hosts experienced sustained increases in memory utilization and token latency for short windows (~3–7 minutes). Investigation shows the KV-store's TTL application path intermittently stalled which delayed eviction decisions and produced an "eviction-window jitter" effect where live working sets briefly exceeded target capacity.

What happened (high level):
- Around 2025-02-18 02:13 UTC we saw a cluster-wide spike in request rate for a small cohort of customers and a concurrent bump in slab compaction activity on several GPU nodes.
- The slab compaction job acquired a global compaction lock which caused the eviction-sampling thread to stall for ~60–240s on affected hosts.
- During the stall TTL metadata updates queued up; when sampling resumed a burst of eviction activity created short-lived pressure on allocator & network (replication) paths, temporarily increasing latency and causing a handful of requests to fallback to slower model variants.
- A recently shipped rate-limiter change (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1189) increased the per-shard lock hold time under contention which exacerbated the stall window.

Root cause hypothesis and evidence:
1) Slab compaction code path takes a compaction lock which, under high allocation churn, can block the eviction-sampling goroutine. Logs from 02:12–02:16 show repeated stack traces with compaction lock held.
2) Eviction-sampling was single-threaded per shard; when it stalls TTL application and score decay are effectively paused. Telemetry shows TTL-applied counters stopped incrementing for the affected shards during the stall windows.
3) The rate-limiter PR increased lock hold times in high contention cases; profiling on a repro host shows 30–45% of CPU while holding the allocator lock during the incident period.

Impact:
- Short-lived capacity overshoot on ~12 hosts across two regions.
- ~64 requests experienced latency >500ms and 6 consumer fallbacks to backup model variants.
- No data loss or request silent failures; correctness preserved.

Action items (proposed):
- Short term (P0/P1):
  - Add eviction-sampling watchdog: if sampling blocked >5s emit high-severity alert + sample stacks (owner: Marcus Chen, estimate: 2).
  - Revert or patch the allocator lock-duration regression from PR 1189 to reduce hold time under contention (owner: Lina Rodriguez, estimate: 3).
  - Add telemetry: per-shard "ttl-applied" heartbeat and compaction-lock hold histogram for 90d retention (owner: Observability, estimate: 3).
- Mid term (P2):
  - Parallelize eviction-sampling across multiple worker goroutines per shard to avoid single-thread stalls (owner: Runtime team, estimate: 8).
  - Make slab compaction incremental to avoid holding the global lock for long windows (owner: Storage infra, estimate: 8).
- Long term (P3):
  - Evaluate lock-free or read-optimized TTL metadata propagation (research task; owner: Research/Applied ML, estimate: 13).

Testing and validation plan:
- Build a synthetic load test that reproduces allocation churn + compaction interplay; validate fixes under stress.
- Add chaos test that temporarily pauses eviction-sampling to confirm watchdog and fallback behaviors.

Artifacts and observability:
- Incident dashboard: https://dash.redwood-inference.internal/d/kv/ttl-eviction-incident-2025-02-18
- Repro harness: internal/ghe/runtime/tests/kv_compaction_repro (PR queued: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1195)
- Post-incident retrospective notes: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/ttl-eviction-2025-02-18

Acceptance criteria (done):
- Watchdog alert firing in staging and production for simulated stalls
- Decrease in compaction lock hold times in the patched build by >60% under reproduction load
- No regression in throughput or median latency in canary before promoting changes to runtime-1.19
